name: Cupid Ltd
tagline: The exact trusted user who queued this stock has since fully exited, citing extreme overvaluation and a suspicious bulk-deal pattern tied to the new promoter
business_overview: Cupid is an Indian manufacturer of male/female condoms, lubricants, and other sexual-wellness/FMCG products, which underwent a change in controlling ownership (Aditya Halwasiya, a 60-year family business group, acquiring a controlling stake) and then rallied roughly 8-9x over the past year on turnaround/expansion hopes.
fundamentals_table: 46.24% (as of Jun 2026), with prior reports of a meaningful pledge percentage
fundamentals_narrative: ROCE/ROE are genuinely strong on paper (33.5% / 27.3%), but this is now almost entirely a valuation and governance story, not a fundamentals story: at a Rs 38,266 Cr market cap against Rs 484 Cr TTM sales and Rs 137 Cr TTM profit, the stock trades near 280-340x earnings after an ~8-9x one-year rally. Even the trusted user whose earlier portfolio mention queued this stock did the math (in-thread) and concluded that even tripling revenue in 5 years plus 20 years of 20% growth thereafter still would not justify the current price.
technical_read: Not pulled this pass — the 52-week range alone (Rs 32.87 to Rs 299, i.e. ~9x) tells the technical story; this is a parabolic small-cap-to-massive-cap re-rating, the kind of move that historically carries elevated reversal risk.
sentiment_summary: Read 100 of 1,567+ posts (2 batches) across the most recent, most active stretch of this thread (posts #1597-1704). This is NOT a simple bullish endorsement — it is a thread actively working through a serious governance concern in real time, with the community's two most engaged trusted contributors both fully exiting their positions during the window read.
community_signal: dineshssairam (trusted, thread contributor and the exact user whose OLD 2020-2021 portfolio backfill queued this stock as very-high) posted TWO critical, recent updates directly in this thread: (1) post #1629 — flagged a 'suspicious surge in Bulk Deals' over the prior 6 months, naming four West-Bengal-registered private companies (with specific director names and addresses) that together bought over 3% of Cupid, a classic circular-ownership/pump pattern; (2) post #1658 (34 loves, the highest-engagement post read) — announced he has 'completely exited Cupid @ 14x from the Average Cost,' explicitly citing extreme overvaluation math that doesn't work even under generous long-term growth assumptions. Separately, Chandragupta (trusted) also fully exited (post #1668), citing Cupid's Rs 50 Cr purchase of TFCI shares as a capital-allocation red flag ('you never know what Cupid's cash surplus will be used for'). GautamBafna (trusted) shared media reports (post #1681) that the Enforcement Directorate suspects a financier linked to promoter Aditya Halwasiya's circle (Hari Tibrewala) of being a hawala operator who has manipulated small-cap share prices, in an article specifically discussing Cupid. Marathondreams (trusted) separately noted 'new owners are using all the levers available to them to prop up the stock price... not a good sign for long term investors.'

trusted_signals.note: Four independent trusted users converged on caution/exit within the same recent stretch of the thread: suspicious bulk-deal pattern (dineshssairam), questionable capital allocation into TFCI (Chandragupta), ED/hawala allegations against a promoter-linked financier (GautamBafna), and stock-price-propping concerns (Marathondreams). dineshssairam and Chandragupta both fully exited. This directly supersedes the original 2020-2021 portfolio-backfill mention that queued this stock.

bse_notes: No confirmed formal SEBI/ED action against Cupid or its promoter directly found — the ED-related reporting concerns an associated financier (Hari Tibrewala) in Aditya Halwasiya's orbit, and the bulk-deal pattern is a community-flagged concern (with named entities/addresses) rather than a regulatory finding. Given the severity, specificity, and convergence of these concerns from multiple trusted users, this is classified as HIGH CAUTION rather than a confirmed EXCLUDE.
bull_case: Genuinely strong ROE/ROCE and a real underlying business (sexual wellness/FMCG) with a credible new promoter narrative around capacity expansion and US FDA approval pathway
New promoter (Aditya Halwasiya) has articulated a coherent growth vision (tripling capacity, entering new markets) in concalls
bear_case: The stock has already rallied ~8-9x in a year to a P/E near 280-340x — the trusted user whose own portfolio mention originally queued this stock has done the valuation math and concluded it doesn't work even under generous assumptions
A specific, named, suspicious bulk-deal pattern (four West-Bengal shell-like entities buying 3%+ combined) was flagged in-thread by a trusted user, a classic small-cap manipulation signature
Media reports link a financier in the new promoter's circle to an ED hawala/share-price-manipulation investigation, specifically naming Cupid in the reporting
Questionable recent capital allocation (Rs 50 Cr into TFCI shares) unrelated to the core business, flagged by a trusted user as a red flag in itself
Two of the most engaged trusted contributors to this exact thread have both fully exited their positions very recently
market_cap_tier: large-cap (post-rally; was small-cap before the run-up)
verdict_headline: The trusted signal that queued this stock has been superseded by the same user's own subsequent, more recent, in-thread reversal — do not treat the old portfolio mention as current
verdict_reasoning: This is a case where the trusted-thread queueing signal (dineshssairam's 2020-2021 portfolio mention) is stale and has been explicitly superseded by that same trusted user's own much more recent posts in the company thread itself — he flagged a suspicious bulk-deal pattern and then fully exited, citing valuation math that doesn't support further upside even under generous assumptions.

This is independently corroborated by three other trusted users (Chandragupta, GautamBafna, Marathondreams) all raising distinct, serious concerns — governance/capital-allocation, promoter-network regulatory scrutiny, and stock-price-propping — within the same recent window, and Chandragupta also fully exited.

Given the severity, specificity, and multi-user convergence of these concerns, this is classified as HIGH CAUTION. Per the project's rules, a red flag always applies regardless of trusted status, so the conviction floor for very-high trusted candidates does NOT apply here — conviction is set to Low.

thesis_fit is 'neither': the stock has already priced in an extraordinary growth scenario (P/E ~280-340x after an 8-9x rally), and the community's own math (from the user who originally flagged this as a holding) concludes further 10x-scale upside isn't credible from here, independent of the governance concerns.
red_flag_reason: Multiple trusted community members (dineshssairam, Chandragupta, GautamBafna, Marathondreams) independently flagged serious concerns within the same recent thread window: a suspicious bulk-deal pattern involving named West-Bengal entities acquiring 3%+ of the company, questionable capital allocation (Rs 50 Cr into unrelated TFCI shares), media reports linking a financier associated with the new promoter to an ED hawala/share-manipulation investigation, and general stock-price-propping concerns. Two of these trusted users have since fully exited their positions.
